papers.title: #524 EEG-based characterization of neurophysiological alterations in mild cognitive impairment during serious game interaction: preliminary results
papers.reason: The study combines EEG, serious-game behavior, and MCI status to characterize neurophysiological alterations, closely matching multimodal cognitive assessment.

papers.title: #471 Association of simultaneous dual-task EEG recordings with global cognitive performance in mild cognitive impairment
papers.reason: Simultaneous dual-task EEG linked to cognitive performance in MCI is a close methodological match to multimodal assessment for cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Initial Psychometric Evaluation of the Riga Cognitive Screening Task (RiTa) in Older Adults with Varying Levels of Cognitive Functioning.
papers.reason: This is relevant to cognitive screening in older adults but provides no stated focus on executive-function mechanisms or multimodal digital biomarkers.

papers.title: Cognitive impairment influences perioperative quality of life in older surgical patients: A multicenter longitudinal study.
papers.reason: The paper uses brief global cognitive screens to predict perioperative quality of life and outcomes without examining executive function or digital assessment.

papers.title: Predictors of change in cognitive function for patients with cancer treated with allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant.
papers.reason: Longitudinal MoCA monitoring addresses clinical cognitive decline, but the analyzed domains and predictors are not specifically centered on executive-function modelling.

papers.title: Transcranial photobiomodulation rebalances cortical excitation/inhibition in young adults with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder
papers.reason: The randomized EEG study identifies frontoparietal neural-dynamic changes that predict working-memory improvement in adults with ADHD.

papers.title: [Use of a rehabilitation glove in the acute phase of ischemic stroke in patients with moderate arm paresis].
papers.reason: Cognitive change is measured only with the global MoCA as a secondary rehabilitation outcome in a study primarily about motor recovery.

papers.title: Narcolepsy-like presentations in intellectual disability with comorbid epilepsy and obstructive sleep apnea: a case-based diagnostic analysis and literature-informed discussion
papers.reason: The case concerns differential diagnosis of sleepiness, epilepsy, and sleep apnea rather than executive-function modelling or cognitive assessment.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Functional Network Responses to Immersive Virtual Reality in Alzheimer Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment: Exploratory Single-Session 3-Group Repeated-Measures Study.
papers.reason: The study compares VR-evoked EEG connectivity and graph measures across AD, MCI, and cognitively normal groups as candidate neurophysiological assessment markers.

papers.title: Systematic Modality Ablation of Multimodal Machine Learning for Predicting 24-Month Progression from Mild Cognitive Impairment to Alzheimer's Disease
papers.reason: The paper systematically evaluates cognitive, imaging, genetic, and fluid biomarkers for predicting MCI progression, although it lacks task, eye-tracking, or EEG measures.

papers.title: Cognitive and behavioral benefits of newspaper reading in community-dwelling older adults: a feasibility randomized controlled trial
papers.reason: The trial measures broad cognitive effects of newspaper reading with MoCA and MMSE but does not isolate or model executive processes.

papers.title: Undetected Cognitive Impairment in Saudi Arabia: A National Analysis of Screening Coverage, Diagnostic Yield, and Equity Gaps in Primary Healthcare.
papers.reason: This health-services analysis concerns national cognitive-screening coverage and equity rather than executive-function measurement or computational modelling.

papers.title: Beyond single-person paradigms: N400 alterations in a social context in schizophrenia
papers.reason: EEG hyperscanning during a Go/NoGo task reveals schizophrenia-related ERP alterations relevant to contextual processing, response inhibition, and cognitive control.

papers.title: A possible association between waist-to-hip ratio and cognitive function among Japanese health-checkup participants: an exploratory cross-sectional study
papers.reason: The study relates an obesity measure to global MoCA performance but does not examine executive mechanisms or specialized cognitive biomarkers.

papers.title: Prêt-à-Jouer: commercial videogames as ready-made human perception labs
papers.reason: The paper proposes commercial games with eye tracking and behavioral timing as ecologically valid platforms for studying human attention and executive functioning.

papers.title: Enlarged perivascular spaces are associated with more severe microstructural damage in white matter lesions among people with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
papers.reason: The title indicates a structural imaging study of white-matter pathology without a stated cognitive or executive-function outcome.

papers.title: Blood pressure change patterns and accelerated cognitive decline: evidence from a national longitudinal cohort of middle-aged and older Chinese adults.
papers.reason: The longitudinal study includes executive-function and memory testing, but its main contribution concerns vascular risk patterns and global cognitive decline.

papers.title: Beyond visual comfort: comparing pupillometry and subjective measures of cognitive strain in workplace lighting
papers.reason: The study validates eye-tracked pupil measures against subjective cognitive load during N-back and writing tasks, directly informing task-based assessment methodology.

papers.title: EEG spectral analysis of nighttime sleep and daytime MSLTs and neurocognitive evaluations in obstructive sleep apnea patients with residual sleepiness.
papers.reason: The paper links distinct EEG spectral patterns to measured deficits in executive function, working memory, vigilance, and selective and sustained attention.

papers.title: Relationships Among Hearing, Auditory Processing, and Cognition: A Study of Older Adults
papers.reason: Auditory processing predicts performance on cognitive screening batteries and may indicate cognitive vulnerability, but executive function is not the central construct.

papers.title: The reducing effect of visuospatial cognitive load on alcohol craving in problematic drinkers
papers.reason: A working-memory load manipulation and eye tracking distinguish automatic orienting from top-down attentional maintenance, providing mechanistic behavioral evidence about executive control.

papers.title: One size fits none: a multi-method evaluation of VR interaction techniques across autistic and neurotypical users
papers.reason: The study combines task behavior, EEG attention and working-memory proxies, and subjective reports to distinguish autistic and neurotypical interaction profiles.

papers.title: Cerebral microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted imaging, cognitive domains, and serum neurofilament light chain in adults with hypertension
papers.reason: The study links vascular brain injury and serum biomarkers specifically to executive, attention, orientation, and visuospatial deficits and evaluates MCI discrimination.

papers.title: A Novel Feedforward Neural Network Model for Accurate Detection of Alzheimer's Disease Using Handwriting Analysis
papers.reason: The paper develops an interpretable classifier using handwriting-derived behavioral biomarkers for inexpensive early detection of Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Reading in adolescents with hearing loss: Slower responses despite neural sensitivity to morphosyntax.
papers.reason: The EEG and behavioral study reports N400/P600 processing effects and a working-memory association, but its core focus is morphosyntax in hearing loss.

papers.title: Natural history and clinical impact of epilepsy in adults with Down syndrome: a multicentre clinical study.
papers.reason: The study tracks epilepsy, EEG abnormalities, and broad cognitive decline in Down syndrome and Alzheimer's disease without analyzing executive-function mechanisms.

papers.title: Moderated mediation of cerebrospinal fluid fibroblast growth factor 21 and KLB rs17618244 genotype in the association between educational attainment and cognitive function.
papers.reason: The biomarker mediation analysis concerns global MoCA performance and education but does not address specific executive processes or digital assessment.

papers.title: Association between periodontal inflammation and cognitive impairment among older adults: A clinical and biomarker-based study
papers.reason: The study associates periodontal inflammation with global cognitive screening scores but offers no specific executive-function or computational assessment component.

papers.title: Cognitive impairment in patients undergoing coronary angiography: a cross-sectional study
papers.reason: The study uses MoCA to characterize general cognitive impairment in coronary disease, with executive and attention deficits reported only as secondary domain findings.

papers.title: Harmonizing Ancient Wisdom with Modern Science: Assessing the Impact of Vedic Chanting on Holistic Health
papers.reason: The title and absence of a summary provide no evidence of executive-function modelling, neuroscience, or cognitive biomarker assessment.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic Signatures of Methylphenidate in ADHD: A Systematic Review and 10 Recommendations for Future Research.
papers.reason: This systematic review identifies task and resting-state EEG signatures of methylphenidate in ADHD, including a consistent P3 effect relevant to attention and higher-order cognitive control.

papers.title: Association between preoperative cognitive impairment and perioperative neurocognitive disorders within 30 days after surgery in elderly patients: a secondary exploratory retrospective analysis
papers.reason: The paper evaluates MoCA as a general clinical predictor of perioperative cognitive disorders without specifically modelling or measuring executive processes.

papers.title: From store to screen: A first step in validating the Dutch Oxford Multiple Errands Test (OxMET-NL) for measuring executive function.
papers.reason: The paper validates a digital, ecologically grounded executive-function task and tests its ability to discriminate acquired-brain-injury patients with functional executive difficulties.

papers.title: Sex-Specific Differences in Response to Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation for Recovery From Post-Stroke Aphasia: A Retrospective Analysis of the NORTHSTAR Trial.
papers.reason: The central outcome is post-stroke language recovery, while executive and visuospatial cognition enter only through secondary MoCA covariates and interpretations.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG biomarkers of general and domain-specific cognitive impairment and plasma P-tau217 in patients with Alzheimer’s disease and mild cognitive impairment
papers.reason: The study combines quantitative EEG, domain-specific cognitive scores, machine learning, and plasma P-tau217 to distinguish controls, MCI, and Alzheimer’s disease.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for Alzheimer's disease characterization using small-sample EEG data
papers.reason: The paper develops an interpretable subject-level EEG classifier for Alzheimer’s disease and identifies frontal theta, posterior alpha, and microstate alterations as candidate digital biomarkers.

papers.title: Cognitive heterogeneity in major depressive disorder: Neuroimaging, transcriptomic, and neurotransmitter profiles.
papers.reason: The multimodal neuroimaging study characterizes broad cognitive heterogeneity in depression but does not isolate executive functions or provide a process model of them.

papers.title: Instrumental activities of daily living in older adults with epilepsy: A cross-sectional and longitudinal multicenter study.
papers.reason: The study links real-world functional impairment in older adults with epilepsy to visuospatial-executive, attention, and memory performance, but executive assessment is not its primary focus.

papers.title: A blood DNA methylation marker of cognitive ability is associated with six-year cognitive performance independent of blood Alzheimer's disease biomarkers.
papers.reason: The title indicates a general blood-based marker of longitudinal cognitive performance but provides no specific connection to executive-function processes or digital assessment.

papers.title: Neurophysiological Characterization of ADHD in Children Using EEG Signals: A Machine Learning Approach to Executive Function Networks
papers.reason: The study uses subject-separated machine learning on EEG spectral features to classify children with ADHD and highlights frontal and frontocentral executive-attention networks.

papers.title: Color Perception in Patients with Schizophreniza and Their Healthy First-degree Relatives: A Cross-sectional Study
papers.reason: The study examines color discrimination as a schizophrenia endophenotype and relates it to global MoCA performance, making executive-function relevance indirect.

papers.title: Working memory operations emerge from dynamic changes in neural subspace geometry
papers.reason: The paper directly reveals how prioritization, deprioritization, and updating reshape human working-memory neural subspaces and relates these dynamics to delta, theta, and aperiodic activity.

papers.title: Menopausal ‘brain fog’ or dementia?—a practical guide for clinicians
papers.reason: This is a broad clinical guide for distinguishing subjective menopausal cognitive symptoms from progressive impairment rather than a study of executive mechanisms or quantitative biomarkers.

papers.title: DTI-ALPS Index and White Matter Disruption Mediate the Link Between Hydrocephalus and Cognitive Dysfunction: An MRI Study.
papers.reason: The study identifies MRI and white-matter pathways associated with cognitive decline in hydrocephalus, including fluency and clock-drawing outcomes, but does not focus specifically on executive mechanisms.

papers.title: Exploring the relationship between mindfulness, prefrontal gamma activity, and working memory performance
papers.reason: The study directly relates working-memory accuracy and retention-period frontal gamma activity measured with task EEG in mindfulness practitioners and controls.

papers.title: Routine Blood Indicators Combined With Sleep Questionnaires for the Identification of Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson's Disease: A Cross‐Sectional Study With a Leakage‐Free Nested Modeling Framework
papers.reason: The study builds a carefully validated multimodal classifier for general MoCA-defined cognitive impairment in Parkinson’s disease but does not specifically assess executive function or use behavioural-task or neurophysiological signals.

papers.title: Selenium and vitamin D3 as potential predictive biomarkers of alcohol dependence syndrome severity: a case-control study.
papers.reason: The paper primarily evaluates blood biomarkers of alcohol dependence and only includes global MoCA impairment as an ancillary clinical measure.
